title: Reinforcing vs. Balancing Loop Simulator
description: Compare a reinforcing loop's runaway growth curve against a balancing loop's goal-seeking convergence, side by side.
creator: Systems Thinking in the Age of AI
author: Dan McCreary
subject: Systems Thinking in the Age of AI
Causal Loop Diagram Notation and Loop Identification
chapter_title: Causal Loop Diagram Notation and Loop Identification

educational.learningObjective: Given animated behavior-over-time graphs, the learner will compare the characteristic signature of a reinforcing loop against that of a balancing loop.
prerequisites: Can classify a loop as reinforcing or balancing
learningOutcomes: Recognize a reinforcing loop from its behavior-over-time signature
Recognize a balancing loop from its convergence toward a goal
Predict loop type from a behavior graph alone
educational.assessmentOpportunity: Show learners an unlabeled behavior-over-time curve and ask them to name the loop type and justify it from the shape.

pedagogical.interactionPattern: Parameterized side-by-side simulation with time-series output
pedagogical.instructionalStrategy: Contrasting cases - two structures run under identical conditions
pedagogical.feedbackType: Animated curves that redraw on every parameter change
misconceptionsAddressed: That reinforcing loops always grow rather than also collapsing
That a balancing loop stops the system rather than steering it
discussionQuestions: Why does a balancing loop settle at a value rather than at zero?
What real systems show an accelerating curve, and how long can that last?
If you only had the behavior graph and not the diagram, what could you still infer?
